projects.title: Space Channel 5 Native (Dreamcast recompilation)
projects.game: Space Channel 5 (USA Dreamcast supported GDI revision)
projects.platform: USA Dreamcast GDI revision → Windows x64, Linux x64/ARM64, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon
projects.status: Preview release v0.1.0-preview.2 (2026-09-17). The README reports Windows gameplay and regression testing, and Linux/macOS build and runtime checks; hands-on Linux/macOS gameplay, graphics, audio, and controller testing remains pending. The importer accepts only the supported USA Dreamcast GDI revision, identified by executable hashes; other regions, revisions, and disc formats are unsupported. GitHub reports the repository is not archived and was last pushed 2026-09-17.
projects.summary: Unofficial native desktop port of the USA Dreamcast game. Its SH-4 game code is translated ahead of time into native modules, with no SH-4 interpreter or dynamic-recompiler fallback; Flycast provides device, rendering, and audio components. The player supplies the supported USA GDI and track files.
projects.strategy: Ahead-of-time static recompilation of Dreamcast SH-4 game code into native modules, with Flycast used for device, rendering, and audio components
projects.source_available: Public GPL-2.0-or-later source. The preview release includes precompiled native modules but no original disc assets; users must supply a supported USA Dreamcast GDI and its tracks.

projects.status: Switch NRO release v0.2 is available. Its changelog reports memory, text rendering, and dialog interaction fixes; the README still notes occasional diagonal movement during fast direction changes and does not claim full-game completion. GitHub reports the repository is not archived and was last pushed 2026-07-29.
projects.summary: Loads the original Android arm64 game library and dependencies through a custom ELF loader, Bionic shims, and a fake JNI layer on Nintendo Switch. It reconstructs touch input from Switch controls and supplies a native text-rendering bridge. Users provide the APK and both OBB files; the wrapper source contains no proprietary binaries or assets.
